link.description: A profile link. `label` identifies the row, so renaming one on update means sending `new_label`.
link.$comment: `update` was absent until wave 7: fixing a typo'd URL meant remove + re-add. See the wave 6 storage-keys reference, follow-up 5.

coursework.description: A module or class. Stored as {name, topics}; `course` is the input spelling for `name`.

coursework_topic.description: Alias for `coursework` -- same list, same object shape.

basic_info.description: Update-only singleton for top-level profile fields

club.description: A society or extracurricular. Stored as {name, activities_involved}.

work_skill.description: A skill or technology used in a role. Bare strings on the parent row, like work_highlight.

sections.title: Personal Information
sections.description: Your basic identity and current status
sections.$comment: path: [] addresses the section ROOT -- these seven keys are stored as top-level scalars on profile.json (server.py:1651). Safe because FieldsRenderer spreads the stored object on every write, so a root write updates keys rather than replacing the section. The one profile entity whose vocabulary was already correct.

info.overview: This section captures who you are at a glance. It helps AI assistants address you correctly and understand your current context (student, professional, location, etc.).
tips: Name: Your full legal name as it appears on official documents.
Preferred Name: The name you'd like AI to call you (nickname, first name, etc.).
Current Role: Your primary occupation or status, e.g. 'Final Year Student', 'Software Engineer', 'Freelance Designer'.
Organisation: Your school, university, or employer.
Location: City and country—helps with locale-specific suggestions (holidays, time zones, spelling conventions).
Nationality: Useful for cultural context and language defaults.
Bio: A 2–3 sentence summary of who you are, your interests, and what you're working on. Think of it as your elevator pitch.

field_placeholders.bio: A brief description of who you are...
field_placeholders.name: Your name
field_placeholders.preferred_name: What you'd like to be called

sections.title: Education
sections.$comment: Binds the STORED keys. The vocabulary used to declare `degree`, `field` and `period`, none of which any writer produced -- `period` in particular maps to TWO stored keys (start_year, end_year), so no node could ever have bound it. Corrected in wave 6; see the wave 6 storage-keys reference. `clubs` has no MCP write path at all (no entity, no branch) -- the UI is its only writer, as it already was.

info.overview: Document your educational journey—schools, degrees, and achievements. This helps AI understand your academic background and tailor advice accordingly.
tips: Add one entry per institution or degree (e.g., separate entries for high school and university).
Institution Name: Full official name of the school or university.
Degree Level: e.g., 'High School Diploma', 'BSc', 'MSc', 'PhD'.
Field of Study: Your major, concentration, or programme name.
Status: Whether you're currently enrolled, have completed, or left incomplete.
Years: Start and end (or expected end) years.
Coursework: Key modules or classes you've taken.
Clubs & Societies: Extracurricular involvement.
Highlights: Notable achievements like awards, high grades, leadership roles, or recognitions.

children.title: Highlights
children.placeholder: e.g. Graduated with honours, Led the debate team
children.$comment: Bare strings on both writers (server.py:2559 appends the string itself). item_control:"input" because these are sentence-like -- the retired editor gave each its own editable row, and chips would mean retyping a whole achievement to fix a typo.

children.title: Coursework / Modules
children.$comment: OBJECTS: {name, topics}. The entity's `course` is the INPUT spelling; `name` is what is stored. Until wave 6 execute_modify appended a bare string here while the editor wrote objects, so an AI-added course rendered blank and could never be removed -- `course in coursework` compares a string to a dict. persona_store._normalize coerces legacy strings.

children.title: Clubs & Societies
children.$comment: OBJECTS: {name, activities_involved}. Before wave 6 `clubs` had no entity and no execute_modify branch at all -- the editor was its only writer, so no AI client could read into or out of it. Both added in wave 6.

field_placeholders.degree_level: e.g. High School, Bachelor's, Master's, PhD

sections.title: Work Experience
sections.$comment: `location` and `description` were declared here and written by NOTHING before wave 6 -- not execute_modify, not the editor -- so every value an MCP client sent under them was discarded. Made real in server.py rather than dropped. `period` IS a stored key on this entity, unlike on `education` where the same name was a phantom.

info.overview: List your professional experiences—jobs, internships, placements, and volunteer work. This helps AI understand your skills and career trajectory.
tips: Add one entry per role. If you held multiple roles at the same company, consider separate entries.
Role: Your job title or position.
Company: The organisation you worked for.
Type: e.g., 'Full-time', 'Part-time', 'Internship', 'Placement', 'Volunteer', 'Freelance'.
Period: Date range in a readable format, e.g., 'Jan 2023 – Jun 2024' or 'Summer 2022'.
Highlights: 3–6 bullet points describing what you did and achieved. Focus on outcomes and impact.

children.title: Skills
children.placeholder: e.g. Project management, Python, Public speaking
children.$comment: Bare strings on the parent row, same shape as `highlights` (server.py work_skill branch). Left as CHIPS rather than item_control:"input": these are short, word-like values you add and drop but never revise, and chips show many at a glance -- the opposite of a highlight, which is a sentence where a typo means retyping the lot.

children.title: Highlights
children.placeholder: e.g. Led a team of five, Cut response time by 40%
children.$comment: Bare strings on both writers (server.py:1541). item_control:"input" matches the retired editor, which gave each highlight its own editable row -- see the education node.

sections.title: Contact & Links
sections.description: How to reach you and your online presence

info.overview: Provide ways to reach you and links to your online profiles. AI can use this to reference your portfolio or suggest networking opportunities.
tips: Emails: Add all relevant email addresses and tag their purpose (Primary, Work, School, etc.).
Links: Your portfolio, GitHub, LinkedIn or personal site — label each one.

sections.title: Emails
sections.$comment: Stores `purpose`. The vocabulary declared `label`, which nothing wrote, and omitted `purpose` -- which the add branch REQUIRES (server.py:1418), so no MCP client could add an email. Both corrected in wave 6.

sections.title: Links
sections.$comment: No `update` action on this entity (server.py:1444-1465) -- an MCP client edits a link by removing and re-adding it. The UI edits in place, which is a superset and needs no declaration.

sections.title: Languages
sections.description: Languages you speak and your fluency level
sections.$comment: Stores `fluency`. The vocabulary declared `proficiency`, the third member of get_field(data, "fluency", "level", "proficiency") -- an input alias that is never persisted. ProfileEditor.jsx documented the divergence in a comment and wrote the correct key; the vocabulary was corrected in wave 6.

info.overview: Languages you speak and your fluency level. This helps AI communicate with you appropriately and understand your linguistic capabilities.
tips: Add one entry per language.
Fluency: native, fluent, conversational or basic.
